transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time, it's probably not a huge deal, but... well, what finally pushed me to make an appointment is that I've been having a little trouble just... staying in my chair when I really should be. 

Like, during our longer sprint planning meetings at work, or recently we had these important mortgage calls. I know I'm supposed to just sit and listen, but I'll suddenly feel like I absolutely need to go grab a glass of water, or I'll just decide I need to check something in the other room right that second. It's a bit embarrassing, honestly, because I really don't want to seem unprofessional or rude to anyone. I just keep getting up even when I know I should stay put. 

Does... does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you can help with?
Do you feel restless when you have the urge to get up during these meetings or calls?

Um, yes, exactly. I try really hard to be polite and just sit calmly on the outside, especially when I'm on camera for work. But inside, there's just this... this pressure building up. 

It feels like I desperately need to move, or switch to a different task, or at least do something with my hands. If I force myself to just sit there for too long, I start feeling like I'm going to crawl out of my skin. I'm sorry, I know that sounds a little dramatic, I really don't mean to overstate it! It's just... a very uncomfortable feeling. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Do you find it hard to focus on what's being discussed during those meetings or calls when you feel the urge to get up?

Um, well... I guess I do sometimes lose my place a little bit? But I'm sure everyone does that, right? It's not that I don't care about what's going on! I really do try to pay attention. 

It's just, like... I can start reviewing a pull request at work, or reading through those mortgage documents with really good intentions. I'll be totally ready to focus. But then after a few minutes, I'll realize I've just been staring at the exact same section, and my mind is somehow thinking about five completely unrelated things all at once. 

It's probably just normal fatigue, though, right? I mean, nobody's perfect at focusing 100% of the time... I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just slacking off, because I really am trying my best. Am I making sense?
Do you feel anxious when you have the urge to get up during these meetings or calls?

Um, anxious? No, I don't think it's anxiety. I mean, I'm not worried about anything bad happening, or feeling stressed about the actual work or the calls. 

It's really just... physical, I guess? Like that restless feeling I mentioned. I'm not sitting there feeling nervous or panicked, I just... really, really want to stand up. Or stretch. Or just do something else. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm having panic attacks or anything like that, because I'm definitely not. I'm generally a pretty happy person! It's just this one little annoying thing with sitting still. Is that helpful?
Have you had trouble sitting still for as long as you can remember, even when you were a kid?

Um, well... I guess, looking back, I was maybe a little bit like this as a kid, too? But I think I was just a really enthusiastic child! I really don't want to sound like I was a bad kid or a troublemaker, because I wasn't, I promise. I always wanted to do well in school.

It's just... I do remember in elementary school, my teachers would sometimes have to move my desk, or, you know, gently remind me to stay in my seat. I was just always so eager to participate! I'd pop up out of my chair, or sometimes I'd accidentally talk before I was called on... just because I was excited about the lesson, you know? And I guess I would rush through my work sometimes, even when I totally understood it, just to get to the next thing. 

But that's pretty normal for kids, right? Just having a lot of energy? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was totally out of control. I really did try to be a good student. Does that answer your question okay?
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Act on impulse? Um... no, I really don't think so. I try to be very careful and responsible with my choices. 

As a software developer, you kind of have to think things through before you execute anything, right? So I definitely don't just jump into decisions blindly. I would really hate for anyone to think I'm careless or reckless! I mean, sure, maybe I'll occasionally, like, grab a coffee I didn't plan on buying, but nothing major at all. 

I always try my very best to be thoughtful about what I'm doing and how it affects things. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm answering these right!
Do you notice that your urge to get up and move is triggered by certain emotions?

Emotions? Um... no, I really haven't noticed anything like that. I don't think it's tied to my feelings at all. 

I wouldn't want you to think I get upset or angry and then have to pace around or anything! I'm actually a very even-keeled person, I promise. It just sort of happens even when I'm perfectly happy or just having a completely normal, calm day at work. It really is just that physical restlessness I mentioned earlier, completely out of the blue. 

I hope I'm explaining this right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, so please let me know if you need me to clarify anything!
Did you have difficulty with sitting still or restlessness as a child, even outside of a school setting?

Um... outside of school? I really don't think so. I don't remember anything like that, anyway. 

I was actually a very well-behaved kid at home, I promise! I always listened to my parents and followed the rules. I mean, sure, I liked to play outside and run around the neighborhood, but that's just normal kid stuff, right? I definitely wasn't, like, running wild through the house or refusing to sit at the dinner table or anything that would cause trouble for my family. I really tried to be good and make things easy for my parents. 

So, no, I don't think I was unusually restless at home or anywhere else. Does that help? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most accurate picture, I hope I'm not missing anything you're looking for!
Have you experienced this restlessness and urge to get up throughout your entire life, or has it developed more recently?

Um... my whole life? No, I don't think so. I mean, maybe I've always liked staying busy, but nothing disruptive, I promise! 

It's really just been... well, maybe the last two years or so? It's just been noticeably harder to manage recently. We took on a mortgage about two years ago, and, you know, there was just so much extra paperwork and planning and sitting down to sort through details that came with it. I think all that extra adult responsibility just made it a little trickier for me to stay put. 

But I'm still staying on top of everything, really! I definitely don't want you to think I'm dropping the ball on my house or anything. It's just that the urge to get up has been a bit more obvious to me since then. Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for? I hope that makes sense!
Did you experience significant restlessness or difficulty staying still before the age of 12?

Um... before I was 12? Well... I guess maybe a little bit, but nothing terrible, I promise! I wasn't a bad kid or anything. 

I do remember, um, in elementary school, my teachers would sometimes have to move my desk? Or they'd remind me to stay seated. I guess I was always popping up out of my chair, or I'd blurt out answers before they called on me. And I tended to rush through my assignments, even when I totally understood the work. But I was just really eager to participate and get things done, you know? I definitely wasn't trying to be disrespectful or cause trouble for the teachers. 

So, I guess there was some of that when I was younger, but I really tried my best to be a good student. Does that answer your question? I hope I'm not making it sound like I was a huge problem in class!
Have you ever had to take a break from work or social activities because you couldn't sit still or focus?

Um... take a full break? Oh, no, I would never just walk away from my responsibilities like that, I promise! I always try my best to push through. 

But... well, I guess it has started causing just a little bit of friction lately? At work, and at home, too. It's just that people have had to follow up with me a bit more than they used to. I guess because I'm up and about or jumping between things, some of the details slip. I really worry that I'm starting to look like the unreliable one when it comes to planning tasks, which is an awful feeling because I am trying *so* hard to keep everything running smoothly. 

I really don't want to let my team or my family down, you know? I'm still getting things done, I just... I worry I'm frustrating people by needing those extra reminders. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for.
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with friends, family, or coworkers because of your difficulty sitting still or focusing?

Um, well... I guess I sort of just mentioned this, but... yeah, there has been a little bit of friction? Not big fights or anything! I promise I'm not, like, arguing with my coworkers or my husband. 

It's just... well, because I'm always kind of moving around or bouncing from one thing to another, I think I miss things. So people at work, and my husband at home, they've had to start checking in on me more? Just to make sure I followed through on things we talked about. I really, really hate it because I feel like they're starting to see me as the unreliable one, especially when it comes to organizing or planning things. 

I'm trying so hard to keep up with everything, I really am. I just... I worry I'm letting them down when they have to keep reminding me. I hope I'm not sounding like a terrible employee or partner... is that what you meant by problems in relationships?
Have you experienced difficulty sitting still or restlessness in situations other than work meetings or mortgage calls?

Um... other situations? Like, besides work or those calls? Well... I guess I'm generally pretty good at holding it together, you know? I really try to be respectful of whatever situation I'm in. 

I don't think there's really anywhere else where it's a big issue. I mean, maybe I tap my foot a little at dinner, or I get up to grab things a lot when we're watching a movie at home, but... that's just normal, right? I don't think I'm making a scene anywhere or being disruptive in public. I really try to be mindful of the people around me. 

So, no, I don't think I have any major problems with it in other places. I hope that's okay? I just really haven't noticed it being a big thing outside of the stuff we already talked about.
Did you experience significant restlessness or difficulty staying still before the age of 7?

Um... before age seven? Gosh, that's going back a ways. I mean, I think I was a pretty good kid! I always wanted to make my teachers happy. 

But... well, I guess my mom has mentioned that kindergarten and first grade were a little... active for me? I don't think I was bad or anything! But I do remember my teachers having to move my desk a few times. Or they'd have to remind me to stay in my seat, because I guess I was always popping up to look at things or talk to people. 

And, um, I think I had a habit of blurting out answers before they called on me. Not to be rude! I just... I would get so excited that I knew the answer, and it just sort of slipped out. And I'd rush through my worksheets, even when I knew how to do the math or whatever, just to be done so I could go do something else. 

I really wasn't trying to be a troublemaker, I promise. I just had a lot of energy back then. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was an awful student? Is that the kind of thing you're looking for?
Did you have symptoms of restlessness or difficulty staying still before you were 12 years old?

Um, yeah, I think I just mentioned this, actually? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much! But yes, definitely before I was twelve. That was right around the time I was in elementary school, and like I said, I was always kind of popping out of my seat. 

My teachers were always so nice about it, but they did have to move my desk a few times. And I'd get so eager to participate that I'd blurt things out before they called on me. I really wasn't trying to be disruptive, I just couldn't hold it in! And I'd rush through my worksheets, even when I knew all the answers, just because I wanted to move on to the next thing. 

I really tried to be a good student, though! I hope that makes sense? I just had a bit more energy than some of the other kids, I guess. Is that what you mean by before twelve?
Did you experience significant restlessness or difficulty staying still before you started elementary school?

Um... before elementary school? Like, preschool age? Gosh... I really don't think so. I mean, my mom has never said anything about me being a difficult toddler or anything like that. 

I think I was just a normal, happy little kid, you know? I liked playing and running around, sure, but... isn't that just what little kids do? I don't think I was unusually restless or anything that would be considered a problem. I always tried to be a good girl for my parents. 

So... no, I don't think I had any issues with that before I started school. I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just really don't remember it being an issue that early on.
Did you exhibit any symptoms of restlessness or difficulty staying still between the ages of 4 and 6?

Um, four and six? I guess that kind of overlaps with what we were just talking about, right? With kindergarten and first grade? 

Like I said, I really don't think I was a problem child before I started school. My parents always said I was a sweet little girl. I mean, maybe when I was five or six, in kindergarten, I started getting a little more... enthusiastic? That's when the teachers would have to remind me to sit down, like I mentioned. 

But at four? No, I don't think so. I was just a normal kid playing. I really hope I'm not making it sound like I was out of control or anything! I just... I think the school environment was a little new to me, and I just wanted to be involved in everything. Does that sound normal for that age? I really tried my best to be good!
Have you experienced difficulty sitting still or feeling restless in multiple different settings or situations?

Um, multiple settings? Like... everywhere? Oh, gosh, no, definitely not. I really try to keep things appropriate depending on where I am. 

I mean, at work—I'm a software developer, so I'm at my desk a lot—I might tap my foot or shift around in my chair a bit, but I'm definitely not, like, pacing around or disrupting the office. I would be so embarrassed if I bothered my coworkers! And at home, I guess I like to get up and fold laundry or tidy things while I'm watching TV, but I always just thought of that as being productive, you know? 

I really do my best to be respectful of my environment and the people around me. I hope I'm not coming across as someone who can't behave in public or anything! I usually keep it pretty contained. Does that answer your question okay?
Is your difficulty staying still mostly a problem when you're at work or doing tasks that require a lot of focus?

Um, mostly at work? No, I wouldn't say it's just there. I mean, I definitely feel it when I'm trying to focus on code for hours, but... it's not like it completely goes away when I leave the office. 

Even if I'm just out to dinner with friends or sitting through a long movie, I still get that urge to shift around or stretch my legs. I try really hard not to be distracting, though! I'll just discreetly bounce my knee under the table or excuse myself to the restroom for a minute just to walk a little. 

So it's not just work tasks, it kind of pops up in other places too. But like I said, I always try to manage it so it doesn't bother anyone else. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were looking for? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Did you exhibit any symptoms of restlessness or difficulty staying still before you were 7 years old?

Um, before I was seven? So, like, kindergarten and first grade? I think we touched on this a little bit already, but... yeah, I guess so. 

I mean, I wasn't a bad kid! I really want to make that clear. I was just... eager, I suppose. I remember in early elementary school, the teachers would sometimes have to move my desk, or they'd gently remind me to stay in my seat. I was just always popping up to see what was going on, or I'd blurt out an answer before they called on me. I just got so excited to participate, you know? 

And I'd kind of rush through my worksheets, even when I totally understood the material, just because I wanted to move on to the next thing. But they always said I was bright! It wasn't malicious or anything, I just had a lot of energy. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a troublemaker. Does that make sense? I was just a really enthusiastic little girl!
